sections.title: Identification and habitat
sections.text: The catalogue entry represents Solanum nigrum, black nightshade, not deadly nightshade. This annual or short-lived perennial often grows on disturbed ground; its height varies widely, from about 5 cm to 1.5 m.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The leaves are about 2.5–9.5 × 1.8–6 cm. The white star-shaped flowers have yellow anthers. Ripe berries are usually dull black-purple and 5–10 mm across.

sections.title: Toxicity and uses
sections.text: Toxicity varies among populations and with maturity; green fruits and other green parts may contain toxic glycoalkaloids. Some sources report eating ripe black fruits, but the species complex and identification risks make foraging hazardous. Consume only reliably identified and prepared food products.
